name: Sales forecast
summary: A weekly sales forecast: commit, best case, closed this quarter and pipeline, with the quota set as the target of Commit and the gap to it and pipeline coverage worked out, a dashboard and a deck for the weekly meeting and a Workflow that asks on Monday and has the sales lead approve.

whatItsFor.text: For a sales team that calls its quarter every week. On Monday the figures for the week just ended come in, the sales lead approves them, and everyone reads the same **commit**, gap to quota and pipeline coverage.
For the weekly forecast meeting it brings:

items: A **dashboard** with this week's call against quota, the change on last week and the last 13 weeks.
A **deck** of seven slides that fills in its own figures.
A **Workflow** that asks, has each value approved, locks the week and sends its Snapshot to the people you pick.
n8n templates that send figures from HubSpot, Salesforce, Pipedrive, Google Sheets or Microsoft Excel.
An **Owner** installs the Pack, because it holds three Themes. An Owner or Admin sets it up.
The team's **quota** for the quarter. You set it once, as the target of **Commit**; nobody sends it every week.
Who calls **Commit** and **Best case** each week.
Where **Closed this quarter** and **Pipeline value** come from: your CRM or a sheet through n8n, or a person who types them.
Decide who approves. Nobody approves their own value while someone else can. The approver needs to be a member of the Workspace, and is picked during Set up.
Room for **9 Metrics** in your Workspace's size, or 8 without **Quota split**.
The money figures are in euro. If yours differ, change the **Unit** with **Edit details…** on each Metric's **Description** tab.

firstSteps.text: Do these in order. After that the week runs by itself.

items: Open **Settings**, then **Packs**. Under this Pack, choose **Set up from this Pack**.
Keep the Metrics ticked, with the dashboard and the Workflow **Weekly sales forecast**. Untick **Quota split** if you do not want the table of the gap by salesperson.

If you send **Commit** and **Best case** yourself, leave **Make me the Submitter of their values** ticked, else untick it. Closed this quarter and Pipeline value are marked as sent by a CRM, so you are not made their Submitter. To type them too, also tick **Ask me also for** them.
Pick the **Approver**, usually the sales lead. Setting up sends no request unless you tick **Send the first requests now**. Choose **Set up**.
Set the quota: open **Commit**, go to the **Targets** tab and give every week of the quarter the quarter's quota. **Paste from a spreadsheet** takes the weeks in one go.

To connect a CRM or a sheet, choose **Fill from n8n** under your system on the page Set up shows, before you choose **Done**. It gives you the file for n8n. Later, the same button is under **Who submits** on the **Description** tab of a Metric.
If someone else sends figures, open the **Setup Guide** from **Help**, choose **Team**, and under **Who is asked for what** pick that person for each of their Metrics and press **Ask**.
Send this week's figures: whoever submits opens each Metric and chooses **Record a value**, or answers the request the Workflow sends. The Approver then approves them.
Open **Decks**, choose **From a Deck Template**, pick **Weekly forecast meeting** and a Metric for each Slot. Each Slot is named like the Metric it takes.
Open the Workflow **Weekly sales forecast**. In its **Send Snapshot** step pick the dashboard **Weekly forecast meeting** and the people who get it, then choose **Save workflow**.
Share that dashboard with those people. Someone who cannot open it is not sent the link.
On Monday Ziffr asks the people who send figures for the week just ended, and the n8n templates send theirs. The figures are due on Tuesday, with a reminder that day.
The Approver approves each value. It is then published and the week is locked.
Before the meeting, open the deck and write what only you know over the questions on its slides, such as why the pipeline moved and what you ask for.
Once the week is finished, the people you picked get a link to its Snapshot.
When a new quarter starts, add its weeks and quota on **Commit**'s **Targets** tab.

eachPart.text: The figures that come in each week

items: **Commit**: what the team commits to closing by the end of the quarter, deals already won included. Its target is the quota.
**Best case**: what the quarter reaches if the open deals that may still close do, deals already won included.
**Closed this quarter**: the value of the deals won since the quarter began. It starts again from 0 each quarter.
**Pipeline value**: all open deals that can still close this quarter, those in the commit included, those already won not.
**Quota split**: optional. The quota by salesperson, only for the deck's slide on where the gap sits.
**Quota**: read from the target of **Commit** for the week.
**Commit gap to quota**: Commit minus the quota. Below 0, the commit is that much short.
**Commit as share of quota**: Commit as a percentage of the quota. 100 % or more covers it.
**Pipeline coverage**: Pipeline value divided by what is still missing, which is the quota minus Closed this quarter. 3 times means the open deals are worth three times what is missing.
The dashboard **Weekly forecast meeting**: the call against quota, the change on last week, the last 13 weeks and the latest commit by salesperson.
The deck **Weekly forecast meeting**: a cover, the call, where the gap sits, the change since last week, the weeks of the quarter, pipeline coverage, and the risks and asks.

The Workflow **Weekly sales forecast**: asks on Monday, reminds on Tuesday, tells the Metric's owner about a missing value on Wednesday, marks a change of more than 25 % as unusual, has every value approved, locks the week and sends its Snapshot.
**Forecast Navy**, **Forecast Coral** and **Forecast Forest**: three Themes. The deck starts with Navy. Add your logo to the Theme you use under **Themes** in **Settings**.

questions.text: Can the figures come from our CRM?

Yes. n8n can send **Closed this quarter** and **Pipeline value** every Monday from HubSpot, Salesforce or Pipedrive, for the team and for salespeople with Metrics of their own. HubSpot and Salesforce can also send **Commit** and **Best case** if you switch them on; Commit is otherwise a person's call. n8n runs on your side, and Ziffr never holds your CRM login.
Can they come from a spreadsheet, or can we type them?

Both. **Fill from n8n** also offers Google Sheets and Microsoft Excel templates, and any figure can be typed by a person who submits it. Figures of earlier weeks can be brought in with **Paste values**.
Which week does a figure belong to?

Each week holds the figures as they stood at its end. A reply to Monday's request counts for the week just ended. In a week that spans two quarters, send the figures of the quarter the week starts in.
How do I see figures by salesperson?

Send the team's figure with a **Breakdown**, one line for each salesperson, such as Ana 205,000, and leave the value empty so the lines are added up. Send all lines together: a newer value replaces them. The slide on where the gap sits needs the same names on **Commit** and **Quota split**.
Why is a calculated figure empty?
One of its figures, or the quota, is missing for that week: set the week's target on **Commit**. Pipeline coverage is also empty when exactly the quota is closed, and below 0 when more is closed.
I am the only one in the Workspace. Who approves?
You check your own values. If checking every one is more than you want, change the Approve step of the Workflow to **Unusual values only**.
Is this the same as the Sales Pack?
No. The Sales Pack counts a month's leads and deals. Sales forecast is a Pack of its own, and you can have both.

metric.name: Commit
metric.description: The forecast call: what the team commits to closing by the end of the quarter, deals already won in it included. Its target is the team's quota: set it on the Targets tab for each week of the quarter. Taken as it stood at the end of the week: a reply to Monday's request counts for the week just ended, and so does its form link while the request is unanswered. By salesperson: add a breakdown with one line for each person, and leave the value empty to add the lines up.
metric.calculationNote: The value of the deals won this quarter plus the open deals the team commits to closing by its end, as it stands at the end of the week. The further deals that count only in the best case, and deals expected after the quarter, are left out.

metric.name: Best case
metric.description: What the quarter reaches if the open deals that may still close do: commit plus upside, deals already won included. Taken as it stood at the end of the week: a reply to Monday's request counts for the week just ended, and so does its form link while the request is unanswered. By salesperson: add a breakdown with one line for each person, and leave the value empty to add the lines up.
metric.calculationNote: The commit plus the upside: the further open deals that may still close by the end of the quarter, as they stand at the end of the week. Deals already lost and deals expected after the quarter are left out.

metric.name: Closed this quarter
metric.description: The value of the deals won since the quarter began. It starts again from 0 each quarter; a week that spans two quarters belongs to the one it starts in. Taken as it stood at the end of the week: a reply to Monday's request counts for the week just ended, and so does its form link while the request is unanswered. By salesperson: add a breakdown with one line for each person, and leave the value empty to add the lines up.
metric.calculationNote: The value of every deal won from the first day of the quarter to the end of the week, added up. Open deals are not in it, and it starts again from 0 with the next quarter.

metric.name: Pipeline value
metric.description: The value of all open deals that can still close this quarter, those in the commit included, those already won not. Taken as it stood at the end of the week: a reply to Monday's request counts for the week just ended, and so does its form link while the request is unanswered. By salesperson: add a breakdown with one line for each person, and leave the value empty to add the lines up.
metric.calculationNote: The full value of every deal still open at the end of the week that can close this quarter, not weighted by its chance. Committed deals that are still open are in it; deals already won and deals expected after the quarter are not.

comesFrom.note: Optional, only for the deck's slide on where the gap sits.

metric.name: Quota split
metric.description: The quota split by salesperson, only for the deck's gap by salesperson slide: each one's quota for the quarter, sent as a breakdown with the same names as Commit's, in every week you want that table. The team's quota everywhere else is the target of Commit. Leave it out at Set up if you do not want the table. Taken as it stood at the end of the week: a reply to Monday's request counts for the week just ended, and so does its form link while the request is unanswered.
metric.calculationNote: The quota of each salesperson for the whole quarter, not a weekly share, sent as one line for each person under the same names as in the breakdown of Commit. Only the slide with the gap by salesperson reads it: every other figure takes the quota of the team from the target of Commit, so the two are kept in step by hand.

metric.name: Quota
metric.description: The team's quota for the quarter, read from the target of Commit, so nobody sends it. Set it on Commit's Targets tab: the quarter's quota for each of its weeks, so every week keeps its own. A Target Range with only “from” works too, but changing it also changes past weeks. Empty in a week without a Commit.
metric.calculationNote: The target of Commit for the week, which holds the quota of the team for the whole quarter: its Target Series value for that week, or else a Target Range with one number. Nobody sends it, and there is no value in a week without a Commit or without such a target.

metric.name: Commit gap to quota
metric.description: Commit minus the quota, which is the target of Commit, for the week. Below 0, the commit is that much short; 0 or more covers it. Empty until the week has a Commit and a quota.
metric.calculationNote: Commit less its target, which holds the quota, both of the same week. A figure below 0 is what the commit lacks to reach the quota, and there is no value in a week without a Commit or a quota.

metric.name: Commit as share of quota
metric.description: Commit as a share of its target, the quota, for the same week. 100 % or more covers it. Empty until the week has a Commit and a quota, and when the quota is 0.
metric.calculationNote: Commit divided by its target, which holds the quota, in percent, both of the same week. There is no value in a week without a Commit or a quota, or when the quota is 0.

metric.name: Pipeline coverage
metric.description: Pipeline value divided by what is still missing, which is the quota (the target of Commit) minus Closed this quarter. 3 times means the open deals are worth three times what is missing. Empty when a figure, the quota or the week’s Commit is missing or exactly nothing is left to close. Below 0 when more than the quota is closed: then nothing is left to cover.
metric.calculationNote: Pipeline value divided by the target of Commit less Closed this quarter, all of the same week: how many times the open deals cover what is still to be closed. There is no value when a figure or the quota is missing or exactly nothing is left to close, and a value below 0 means that more than the quota is already closed.
